slides.texte_overlay:
5 tiny habits that quietly
protect your mental health

one honest check in

ask yourself once a day how you really feel, and answer honestly. naming your emotions takes away much of their power, and it helps you notice patterns early.

a walk in daylight

take a short walk outside before noon. daylight and movement are two of the most reliable mood lifters there are, and they work faster than you think.

less news before bed

stop reading the news an hour before sleep. your mind can't fix the world at midnight, and it deserves a calm, quiet last hour to rest and recover properly.

something new to think about

spend 5 minutes a day learning something gentle and new: a constellation, a painting, a myth. curiosity gives your mind a peaceful place to go when worries come.

slides.texte_overlay:
a kind word to yourself

say one kind thing to yourself each evening, out loud or in writing. the voice you use with yourself shapes your mental health more than almost anything else.
